question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Snow ______ lightly as everyone was leaving church.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. was falling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The second clause "as everyone was leaving church" is in the past continuous tense. Two actions happening simultaneously in the past must both be shown in the past continuous, so the blank needs "was falling".

◦ Correct: Snow was falling lightly as everyone was leaving church.

• "Snow" is an uncountable singular noun, so the singular auxiliary "was" (not "were") is used.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "falling" is a bare present participle; without a helping verb it cannot work as the finite verb of the clause.

• Option 2 "is falling" is present continuous and clashes with the past-tense clause "was leaving".

• Option 4 "fallen" is the past participle (V3) and needs "had/has/have" before it.

NOTE

• Past continuous = was/were + V-ing. It is used (i) for an action in progress at a past moment, and (ii) for two parallel past actions, usually linked by "while / as / when".

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Satya Nadella completed his primary education ______ Hyderabad Public School, Begumpet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. from.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verbs "complete / graduate / pass out / do one's education" take the preposition "from" before the name of the institution, because the institution is the source of the education.

◦ Correct: Satya Nadella completed his primary education from Hyderabad Public School, Begumpet.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "by" shows the agent or means (a book written by him), not the place of study.

• Option 3 "over" shows position above or duration ("over the table", "over two years").

• Option 4 "onto" shows movement to a surface ("jumped onto the stage") and cannot be used with education.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: study at/in a school, graduate from a university, do a degree in Physics from Delhi University, be educated at Eton.

• Static GK: Satya Nadella, born in Hyderabad, is the Chairman and CEO of Microsoft (CEO since 2014).

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

In the absence of miracles, my frustration spikes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Increases.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As a verb, "spike" means to rise sharply and suddenly; hence its closest synonym here is "increases". (अचानक तेज़ी से बढ़ना)

◦ Example: Prices spiked after the announcement — they increased sharply.

• The sentence means that when no miracle happens, the speaker's frustration shoots up.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Digs" (to break up or turn over ground) is unrelated.

• Option 2 "Falls" (to drop/decrease) is the antonym of spike.

• Option 3 "Losses" is a noun (things lost) and cannot replace the verb "spikes".

NOTE

• Synonyms of spike (verb): increase, surge, soar, shoot up, escalate, rocket. Antonyms: fall, plunge, dip, decline, plummet.

• As a noun, "spike" also means a sharp pointed piece of metal and "a sudden sharp rise on a graph".

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

A blast from the past
option_1: A competition where the outcome is difficult to judge or predict
option_2: Punishment for the crime committed in the past
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Something powerfully nostalgic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a blast from the past" means something (a song, photograph, person, etc.) from an earlier time that suddenly reappears and brings back strong, pleasant memories — i.e., something powerfully nostalgic. (पुरानी यादें ताज़ा कर देने वाली कोई चीज़)

◦ Example: Hearing that 90s song on the radio was a blast from the past.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 describes a "close call / neck-and-neck contest", not this idiom.

• Option 2 wrongly takes "past" literally as a past crime and its punishment.

• Option 4 "an unresolved argument" would be a "bone of contention".

NOTE

• Related idioms of memory/time: "down memory lane" (recalling the past fondly), "a trip down memory lane", "relive old times", "old flame" (a former lover).

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Abolish
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Formalize.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Abolish" means to do away with / put an end to a law, system or practice officially. (समाप्त करना / उन्मूलन करना)

• "Formalize" means to give something official or legal status; to establish it formally — the exact opposite of abolishing it. (औपचारिक/वैध रूप देना)

◦ Example: The government abolished the tax, but later formalized a new levy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Efface" (to rub out, erase, wipe away) is close in sense to abolish — a synonym, not an antonym.

• Option 2 "Deface" (to spoil the appearance of something, e.g., by writing on it) is unrelated.

• Option 3 "Jettison" (to throw away/discard, especially cargo from a ship) is again a synonym of doing away with.

NOTE

• Synonyms of abolish: annul, repeal, revoke, rescind, eradicate, do away with. Antonyms: establish, institute, formalize, create, retain.

• Static link: Sati was abolished in 1829 by Lord William Bentinck; untouchability is abolished by Article 17 of the Indian Constitution.

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: His grip tightend a fractoin on her arm.
option_2: His grip tightened a fraction on her arm.
option_3: His grrip tightned a fraction on her arm.
option_4: His gripe tightened a fracton on her arm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. His grip tightened a fraction on her arm.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All three key words are spelt correctly only in Option 2: "grip" (a firm hold), "tightened" (made tighter) and "fraction" (a very small amount/part).

◦ Correct: His grip tightened a fraction on her arm.

• Spelling keys: GRIP; TIGHT + ENED; FRAC + TION.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 misspells "tightened" as "tightend" and "fraction" as "fractoin".

• Option 3 misspells "grip" as "grrip" and "tightened" as "tightned".

• Option 4 uses "gripe" (to complain / a stomach pain) instead of "grip", and misspells "fraction" as "fracton".

NOTE

• Note the meaning trap: grip (a firm hold) vs gripe (to grumble). "A fraction" used adverbially means "very slightly" — "move a fraction to the left".

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Neweset.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Neweset" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Newest", the superlative of "new" (new – newer – newest). (सबसे नया)

◦ Correct: This is the newest model in the showroom.

• Spelling key: NEW + EST (no extra "e" between).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Drape" (to hang cloth loosely over something), "Vibe" (the mood or atmosphere a person/place gives out) and "Surround" (to be all around something) are all spelt correctly.

NOTE

• Degrees of one-syllable adjectives simply add -er / -est: new–newer–newest, old–older–oldest, tall–taller–tallest. Never insert an extra vowel before "-est".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She was moving slowly and ________ yesterday when she fell.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. shakily.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is joined by "and" to the adverb "slowly", so it must be an adverb that is consistent in sense with slow, unsteady movement that ends in a fall. "Shakily" means in an unsteady, trembling manner. (लड़खड़ाते हुए / काँपते हुए)

◦ Correct: She was moving slowly and shakily yesterday when she fell.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "firmly" and 4 "strongly" suggest steady, powerful movement — they contradict "slowly" and the fall.

• Option 3 "vaguely" means "in an unclear/indefinite way" and is used for thoughts, memories or expressions, not for the manner of walking.

NOTE

• Adverbs of manner from adjectives ending in -y: shaky → shakily, happy → happily, easy → easily (y changes to i before -ly).

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

They must have been more than just suspicious of you.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Definitive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Suspicious" means having or showing doubt/distrust; uncertain about something. (संदेहपूर्ण)

• Its antonym is "definitive", meaning final, conclusive and certain — leaving no room for doubt. (निश्चित / निर्णायक)

◦ Example: The police were suspicious at first, but the DNA report gave a definitive answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Ambiguous" (open to more than one interpretation) keeps the sense of uncertainty — not an antonym.

• Option 3 "Doubtful" is a synonym of suspicious.

• Option 4 "Queer" (strange, odd) does not carry the opposite sense.

NOTE

• Synonyms of suspicious: doubtful, distrustful, sceptical, wary, dubious. Antonyms: definitive, certain, trusting, convinced, unquestioning.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

To treat nightmare disorder, there is a number of medications and therapies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. there is a number.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The expression "a number of" means "many" and always takes a plural verb. Hence "there is a number" must become "there are a number".

◦ Correct: To treat nightmare disorder, there are a number of medications and therapies.

• Contrast: "the number of" takes a singular verb — "The number of medications is large."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "of medications and therapies" is correct — the plural nouns confirm that the verb should be plural.

• "To treat nightmare disorder," is a correct infinitive phrase of purpose.

• Since a clear error exists, "No error" cannot be the answer.

NOTE

• Quantifier–verb agreement: a number of / a lot of / plenty of / a majority of + plural noun → plural verb; the number of / the amount of → singular verb.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

What to do in the event of a gas ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. leak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "gas leak" is the standard collocation for gas escaping accidentally from a pipe or cylinder. (गैस का रिसाव)

◦ Correct: What to do in the event of a gas leak.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "lead" is either a metal (उच्चारण "led") or the verb "to guide" — it does not collocate with gas here.

• Option 2 "leek" is a vegetable of the onion family.

• Option 3 "leer" means to look at someone in an unpleasant, sly or lustful way.

NOTE

• These are classic homophone/near-homophone traps: leak (रिसाव) – leek (सब्ज़ी) – leer (घूरना) – lead (सीसा / नेतृत्व करना). Common collocations: gas leak, water leak, leak of information, leaked documents.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

MLA is a representative electing by the voters of a constituency to the legislature.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. elected by the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The representative does not elect; he is elected. The sentence therefore needs the past participle (passive) form "elected", not the present participle "electing".

• The noun "voters" here is specific (the voters of a particular constituency), so the definite article "the" is required, not "a".

◦ Correct: MLA is a representative elected by the voters of a constituency to the legislature.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "elects by a" makes the representative the doer and is grammatically broken.

• Option 2 "elected by a" gets the participle right but wrongly uses "a" before the plural noun "voters".

• Option 3 "No improvement" is wrong because "electing by the" is clearly incorrect.

NOTE

• Reduced relative clause: "a representative who is elected by the voters" → "a representative elected by the voters". The -ing form shows an active sense; the -ed/V3 form shows a passive sense.

• Static GK: an MLA (Member of Legislative Assembly) is directly elected by voters of a constituency to the State Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha).

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Confirm
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Corroborate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Confirm" means to establish the truth of something; to support or verify it. Its closest synonym is "corroborate", which means to give evidence that supports a statement or theory. (पुष्टि करना / समर्थन करना)

◦ Example: A second witness corroborated/confirmed her account of the accident.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Corrosion" is a noun meaning the gradual eating away of metal by chemical action (rusting).

• Option 2 "Collision" is a noun meaning a crash between two moving bodies.

• Option 4 "Collaborate" means to work together with someone — a common confusion word, but a different meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of confirm: corroborate, verify, substantiate, validate, authenticate, endorse. Antonyms: contradict, refute, deny, disprove.

• Remember the pair: corroborate (to support with evidence) vs collaborate (to work jointly).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

I particular like that kitten because it has white feet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. I particular like.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A verb must be modified by an adverb, not an adjective. "Particular" is an adjective; the verb "like" needs the adverb "particularly".

◦ Correct: I particularly like that kitten because it has white feet.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "that kitten because it" is correct — "because" properly introduces the reason clause.

• "has white feet" is correct — the singular subject "it" takes "has", and "feet" is the correct irregular plural of "foot".

• Since a definite error exists, "No error" is not the answer.

NOTE

• Adjective vs adverb: adjectives qualify nouns (a particular case), adverbs qualify verbs, adjectives and other adverbs (I particularly like it).

• Similar pairs: quick/quickly, strong/strongly, easy/easily, real/really.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Extreme physical or mental sufferings
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Agony.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Agony" means extreme physical or mental suffering / intense pain or anguish. (घोर पीड़ा / यातना)

◦ Example: He was in agony after the accident.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Autonomy" = the right of self-government; independence. (स्वायत्तता)

• Option 3 "Aviary" = a large enclosure for keeping birds. (पक्षीशाला)

• Option 4 "Autocracy" = a system of government by one person with absolute power. (निरंकुश शासन)

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: anguish (severe mental pain), agony (extreme suffering), ecstasy (extreme joy), apiary (place for bees), aquarium (tank for fish), arboretum (place for trees).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

There is no big deal if she didn't came to the party.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. came to the party.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the auxiliary "did / didn't", the verb must be in its base form (V1), never the past form (V2). So "didn't came" is wrong; it must be "didn't come".

◦ Correct: There is no big deal if she didn't come to the party.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "There is no big" and "deal if she didn't" are acceptable in context.

• Since a clear error exists, "No error" cannot be the answer.

NOTE

• Rule: do / does / did / don't / doesn't / didn't + V1. Examples: He didn't go (not went), She doesn't like (not likes), Did you see it? (not saw).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The day are warm, so the students ate their lunch outside.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. was warm.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two corrections are needed:

◦ Subject–verb agreement — "The day" is singular, so it takes "was", not "are".

◦ Tense — the second clause "the students ate their lunch" is in the past tense, so the first clause must also be past.

◦ Correct: The day was warm, so the students ate their lunch outside.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "was warming" (past continuous) wrongly suggests an ongoing process of becoming warm rather than a state.

• Option 2 "is warm" is present tense and clashes with "ate".

• Option 3 "No improvement" is wrong because "The day are warm" is doubly incorrect.

NOTE

• Sequence of tenses: when the main clause is in the past, the connected clauses normally stay in the past too. Also remember singular subject + singular verb (day was), plural subject + plural verb (days were).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Against the clock
option_1: To take on a task that is a way to big
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Rushed and short on time.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "against the clock" means working in a great hurry because very little time is left; racing to finish before a deadline. (समय के विरुद्ध दौड़ / बहुत जल्दी में)

◦ Example: The rescue team worked against the clock to reach the trapped miners.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 describes "to bite off more than one can chew" (to take on too big a task).

• Option 2 describes "on the verge of / within an inch of" success.

• Option 3 describes "to give someone the silent treatment" or "to clam up".

NOTE

• Related time idioms: "beat the clock" (finish before the deadline), "round the clock" (all day and night), "in the nick of time" (just in time), "call it a day" (stop working).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

Don't try to force the window open, or you might broken it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. you might break.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After a modal verb ("might"), the verb must be in its bare infinitive (V1) form. "Broken" is the past participle (V3), so "might broken" is wrong; it must be "might break".

◦ Correct: Don't try to force the window open, or you might break it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "you might breaks" wrongly adds "-s" after a modal — modals are never followed by the -s form.

• Option 2 "you have break" is grammatically broken; it would need "have broken", which also does not fit the warning about a future possibility.

• Option 4 "No improvement" is wrong since the underlined part is clearly incorrect.

NOTE

• Modals — can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must — are always followed by V1 (base form): he may go, she must come, you might break.

• Verb forms: break – broke – broken.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

Beginning to exist; recently formed or developed
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Nascent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nascent" means just coming into existence; newly formed and beginning to develop. (उदीयमान / नवजात)

◦ Example: The country's nascent electric-vehicle industry needs government support.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Herald" = a messenger, or a sign that something is about to happen. (अग्रदूत)

• Option 2 "Blasphemy" = speech or action that shows disrespect towards God or sacred things. (ईशनिंदा)

• Option 3 "Knave" = a dishonest, unscrupulous man; a rogue. (धूर्त व्यक्ति)

NOTE

• Synonyms of nascent: emerging, budding, embryonic, incipient, fledgling. Antonyms: mature, developed, established, declining.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

"I am proud to (1) ______ to a religion which has taught the world both tolerance (2) ______ universal acceptance," he declared (3) ______ September 11, 1893. "We believe not only in universal toleration, (4) ______ we accept all religions as true. I am proud to belong to a nation which has sheltered the persecuted and the (5) ______ of all religions and all nations of the earth."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. belong.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "belong" takes the preposition "to" and means to be a member of / be attached to a group, faith or nation.

◦ Correct: "I am proud to belong to a religion which has taught the world both tolerance and universal acceptance."

• The very next sentence repeats the same structure — "I am proud to belong to a nation ..." — which confirms the answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "live" takes "in/at" for places, not "to a religion".

• Option 3 "behest" is a noun meaning a command or urgent request ("at the behest of"), so it cannot follow "to" as a verb.

• Option 4 "gain" (to obtain) does not fit "gain to a religion".

NOTE

• Static GK: these are the famous opening words of Swami Vivekananda's address at the World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago, on 11 September 1893, delivered as a delegate of Hinduism.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

"I am proud to (1) ______ to a religion which has taught the world both tolerance (2) ______ universal acceptance," he declared (3) ______ September 11, 1893. "We believe not only in universal toleration, (4) ______ we accept all religions as true. I am proud to belong to a nation which has sheltered the persecuted and the (5) ______ of all religions and all nations of the earth."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. and.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correlative pair "both ... and" is fixed in English. Since the sentence already has "both tolerance", the blank must be "and".

◦ Correct: ... a religion which has taught the world both tolerance and universal acceptance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "as well as" cannot follow "both" ("both X as well as Y" is a common but incorrect construction).

• Option 3 "or" would express a choice, contradicting "both".

• Option 4 "also" is an adverb, not a conjunction, and cannot join the two nouns.

NOTE

• Correlative conjunctions (always used in pairs): both ... and, either ... or, neither ... nor, not only ... but also, whether ... or. The items joined must be grammatically parallel.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

"I am proud to (1) ______ to a religion which has taught the world both tolerance (2) ______ universal acceptance," he declared (3) ______ September 11, 1893. "We believe not only in universal toleration, (4) ______ we accept all religions as true. I am proud to belong to a nation which has sheltered the persecuted and the (5) ______ of all religions and all nations of the earth."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With a specific date, the preposition of time used is "on".

◦ Correct: ... he declared on September 11, 1893.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "upon" chiefly indicates position on a surface or immediacy ("upon hearing the news") and is not used for plain dates.

• Option 2 "in" is used with months, years, seasons and centuries — in September, in 1893, in summer.

• Option 4 "at" is used with exact clock times and points — at 5 p.m., at night, at noon.

NOTE

• Prepositions of time: AT — precise time (at 6 o'clock, at night); ON — days and dates (on Monday, on 11 September); IN — longer periods (in July, in 1893, in the morning).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

"I am proud to (1) ______ to a religion which has taught the world both tolerance (2) ______ universal acceptance," he declared (3) ______ September 11, 1893. "We believe not only in universal toleration, (4) ______ we accept all religions as true. I am proud to belong to a nation which has sheltered the persecuted and the (5) ______ of all religions and all nations of the earth."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. but.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the correlative pair "not only ... but (also)". As it begins with "We believe not only in universal toleration", the blank must be "but".

◦ Correct: We believe not only in universal toleration, but we accept all religions as true.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "yet" and Option 2 "though" express contrast/concession and break the fixed "not only ... but" pairing.

• Option 3 "and" is a simple additive conjunction and cannot complete "not only ...".

NOTE

• "Not only ... but also" is used to add emphasis to the second, more important item. If "not only" begins a sentence, inversion follows: "Not only did he speak, but he also sang.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

"I am proud to (1) ______ to a religion which has taught the world both tolerance (2) ______ universal acceptance," he declared (3) ______ September 11, 1893. "We believe not only in universal toleration, (4) ______ we accept all religions as true. I am proud to belong to a nation which has sheltered the persecuted and the (5) ______ of all religions and all nations of the earth."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. refugees.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is paired with "the persecuted" and follows the verb "sheltered". A nation shelters "the persecuted and the refugees" — people who have fled their homelands because of persecution. (शरणार्थी)

◦ Correct: ... a nation which has sheltered the persecuted and the refugees of all religions and all nations of the earth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "toilers" (people who labour hard), 3 "workers" and 4 "peons" (low-grade attendants) all refer to labour, not to people seeking shelter, so they do not match "sheltered ... the persecuted".

NOTE

• Vocabulary: refugee (one who flees to another country for safety), migrant (one who moves for work), asylum seeker (one formally requesting protection), persecuted (harassed or oppressed, especially for religion or race).

question: How many countries share the international land border with India, as of 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of 2022, seven (7) countries share an international land border with India: Bangladesh, China, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan and Afghanistan. (भारत के साथ स्थल सीमा साझा करने वाले 7 देश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Longest land border with India — Bangladesh (about 4,096 km); shortest — Afghanistan (about 106 km).

• Sri Lanka and Maldives share only a maritime boundary with India, not a land border.

• India's total land boundary is about 15,106.7 km.

NOTE

• Important boundary lines: Radcliffe Line (India–Pakistan), McMahon Line (India–China, in the northeast), Durand Line (Pakistan–Afghanistan), LoC (Line of Control in Jammu & Kashmir).

question: Which folk dance of Rajasthan is also known as 'Sapera dance'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalbelia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kalbelia" is the folk dance of Rajasthan performed by the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community, which is why it is popularly called the "Sapera dance" or snake-charmer dance. (कालबेलिया — सपेरा नृत्य)

• The dancers wear flowing black angrakhi and ghagra and their swirling movements imitate a serpent.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kalbelia was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

• Instruments used: been (pungi), khanjari, dholak and morchang.

NOTE

• Other Rajasthani folk dances: Ghoomar (performed by women, especially during Teej and Holi), Gair (performed by men of the Bhil community), Chari (with lighted pots on the head), Kachhi Ghodi and Terah Taali.

question: Which among the following planets does not have any satellite?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Venus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given options, Venus has no natural satellite (moon). In the Solar System, only Mercury and Venus are without moons. (शुक्र — कोई उपग्रह नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Venus is the hottest planet (due to a thick CO₂ atmosphere and runaway greenhouse effect), is called the Morning Star / Evening Star and Earth's twin (similar size and mass); it rotates clockwise (retrograde).

• Jupiter is the largest planet and has the greatest number of known moons (Ganymede, Callisto, Io, Europa — the Galilean moons).

• Saturn is famous for its rings and moons such as Titan; Uranus has moons like Titania and Oberon and also rotates on its side.

NOTE

• Order of planets from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. Earth has one natural satellite — the Moon; Mars has two — Phobos and Deimos.

question: Materials that do not allow electric current to pass through them are called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is insulators.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Insulators" are materials that do not allow electric current to pass through them because they have very few free electrons and very high resistance. (कुचालक / विद्युतरोधी)

• Common examples: rubber, glass, plastic, dry wood, ebonite, mica, porcelain and dry air.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Conductors (copper, silver, aluminium, iron) allow current to flow easily; silver is the best conductor of electricity, though copper is used in wiring for cost reasons.

• A capacitor stores electrical charge; an inductor stores energy in a magnetic field. Neither is defined by blocking current.

NOTE

• Semiconductors (silicon, germanium) lie between conductors and insulators and are the basis of all electronic chips. Electricians' tools have rubber/plastic handles precisely because these are insulators.

question: Who among the following was revered as the 'Queen of Thumri'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Girija Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Girija Devi (1929–2017), the celebrated vocalist of the Banaras (Seniya and Banaras) gharana, was revered as the "Queen of Thumri" (Thumri Queen / Appa ji). (ठुमरी की रानी — गिरिजा देवी)

• She popularised the semi-classical (light classical) forms — thumri, kajri, chaiti, dadra and tappa.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• She was honoured with the Padma Shri (1972), Padma Bhushan (1989), Padma Vibhushan (2016) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

• Siddheshwari Devi was also a great Banaras thumri singer (Girija Devi's senior contemporary), Naina Devi was a well-known thumri exponent and broadcaster, and Annapurna Devi was a legendary surbahar player.

NOTE

• Thumri is a semi-classical vocal form of North India, usually romantic or devotional, associated with Lucknow and Banaras gharanas, and often sung in ragas like Khamaj, Pilu and Bhairavi.

question: Plants with green and tender stems are called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is herbs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Herbs" are small plants with green and tender (soft) stems, usually less than about one metre tall, with few or no branches near the base. (शाक / जड़ी-बूटी वाले पौधे)

• Examples: tomato, wheat, paddy, mint, coriander, mustard, grass.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Shrubs are medium-sized plants with hard, woody stems branching near the base (e.g., rose, lemon, henna).

• Trees are tall plants with a thick, hard woody trunk and branches high above the ground (e.g., mango, neem, banyan).

• Canopy is not a plant type — it is the upper layer of leaves/branches formed by tree crowns in a forest.

NOTE

• Plants are also classified as climbers (weak stems needing support, e.g., money plant, grapevine) and creepers (stems that spread on the ground, e.g., pumpkin, watermelon).

question: Sex ratio in India is defined as the number of females per ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1000 males in the population.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India, the "sex ratio" is officially defined as the number of females per 1000 males in the population. (लिंगानुपात — प्रति 1000 पुरुषों पर महिलाएँ)

• As per Census 2011, India's sex ratio was 943 females per 1000 males.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kerala had the highest sex ratio (1084) and Haryana the lowest (879) among states in Census 2011; among UTs, Puducherry was highest and Daman & Diu lowest.

• Child sex ratio (0–6 years) in Census 2011 was 919 — the lowest since independence, which led to the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (2015) campaign.

NOTE

• Note the difference in convention: many countries express sex ratio as males per 100 females, but India uses females per 1000 males. The next Census will update these figures.

question: The Ravan Phadi cave in _________ is an example of the early Chalukya style architecture which is known for its distinct sculptural style.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ravan Phadi (Ravana Phadi) cave is located at Aihole in the Bagalkot district of Karnataka and is one of the oldest rock-cut caves of the early Chalukyas (6th century CE), famous for its distinctive sculptural style, especially the large Nataraja (dancing Shiva) with the Sapta Matrikas. (रावण फडी गुफा — कर्नाटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Chalukyas of Badami (Vatapi) ruled from the 6th to 8th centuries CE; their greatest king was Pulakeshin II, who defeated Harshavardhana.

• Their architectural sites in Karnataka — Aihole (the "cradle of Indian temple architecture"), Badami and Pattadakal — are celebrated; Pattadakal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Chalukyan temples blend Nagara (North Indian) and Dravida (South Indian) styles, giving rise to the Vesara style. Famous Aihole temples: Durga temple, Lad Khan temple and Huchimalli temple.

question: The 36th meeting of 'Parliamentary committee on official language' was chaired by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amit Shah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 36th meeting of the Parliamentary Committee on Official Language was chaired by the Union Home Minister, Shri Amit Shah, who is the ex-officio Chairman of this Committee. (राजभाषा संबंधी संसदीय समिति — अमित शाह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Committee of Parliament on Official Language was constituted in 1976 under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, to review the progress in the use of Hindi for official purposes and to submit its report to the President.

• It has 30 members — 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.

NOTE

• Article 343 makes Hindi in Devanagari script the official language of the Union; Article 351 directs the Union to promote the spread of Hindi. The Eighth Schedule currently lists 22 languages.

question: The Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021 seeks to increase the marriage age of women to _________ years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 21.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021 seeks to raise the minimum age of marriage for women from 18 to 21 years, making it the same as that for men. (महिलाओं के विवाह की न्यूनतम आयु — 21 वर्ष)

• It was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2021 and referred to a Parliamentary Standing Committee.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Bill amends the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, and is intended to override personal laws and customs.

• It followed the recommendations of the Jaya Jaitly Task Force set up to examine the age of motherhood, maternal mortality and nutrition.

NOTE

• The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 replaced the Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929 (Sarda Act). Child marriage is voidable at the option of the contracting party who was a child.

question: Malgudi Days is a collection of short stories by _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is R.K. Narayana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Malgudi Days" (1943) is a famous collection of short stories by R. K. Narayan, set in the fictional South Indian town of Malgudi. (मालगुडी डेज़ — आर. के. नारायण)

• It was adapted into a much-loved Doordarshan television series directed by Shankar Nag.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other works by R. K. Narayan: Swami and Friends, The Bachelor of Arts, The Dark Room, The English Teacher, The Guide (Sahitya Akademi Award, 1960), The Man-Eater of Malgudi and The Vendor of Sweets.

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan and the Padma Vibhushan.

NOTE

• Other authors listed: Jhumpa Lahiri (Interpreter of Maladies — Pulitzer Prize, The Namesake), Chetan Bhagat (Five Point Someone, 2 States) and Amish Tripathi (The Immortals of Meluha — Shiva Trilogy).

question: Who won India's first badminton medal in Olympics games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saina Nehwal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Saina Nehwal won India's first-ever Olympic medal in badminton — a bronze in the women's singles at the London Olympics, 2012. (सायना नेहवाल — 2012 लंदन ओलंपिक, कांस्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• P. V. Sindhu won silver at Rio 2016 and bronze at Tokyo 2020, becoming the first Indian woman to win two individual Olympic medals; she is also a World Champion (2019).

• Prakash Padukone was the first Indian to win the All England Championship (1980); Pullela Gopichand won it in 2001 and later coached both Saina and Sindhu.

NOTE

• Saina Nehwal became the World No. 1 in 2015 and has won the Padma Shri, Arjuna Award, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna and the Padma Bhushan. Badminton's team events: Thomas Cup (men) — won by India in 2022 — and Uber Cup (women).

question: The period of life, when the body undergoes changes leading to reproductive maturity is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is adolescence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Adolescence" is the period of life when the body undergoes physical and hormonal changes that lead to reproductive maturity. It generally lasts from about 11 to 19 years of age. (किशोरावस्था)

• Adolescents are also called "teenagers"; the changes of this period are collectively called puberty.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Changes at puberty: sudden increase in height, change in body shape, voice change (larynx growth — Adam's apple in boys), increased activity of sweat and sebaceous glands and development of secondary sexual characters.

• Hormones involved: testosterone (male, from testes) and oestrogen (female, from ovaries), controlled by the pituitary gland.

NOTE

• Cloning is the production of a genetically identical copy (e.g., Dolly the sheep, 1996); budding is a form of asexual reproduction seen in Hydra and yeast.

question: Corbillon Cup is associated with which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Table Tennis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Corbillon Cup" is the trophy awarded to the winners of the women's team event at the World Table Tennis Championships. (कॉर्बिलन कप — टेबल टेनिस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The corresponding men's team trophy in table tennis is the Swaythling Cup.

• Table tennis is governed by the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF), founded in 1926; the standard table is 2.74 m × 1.525 m and matches are played to 11 points.

• Indian table tennis stars: Achanta Sharath Kamal, Manika Batra, Sathiyan Gnanasekaran.

NOTE

• Other sports trophies: Thomas Cup / Uber Cup (badminton), Davis Cup / Uber-free Fed Cup (tennis), Ryder Cup (golf), Agha Khan Cup / Beighton Cup (hockey), Ranji Trophy / Duleep Trophy (cricket).

question: Which country is the host of "Vostok-2022" military exercise?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Russia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Vostok-2022" strategic command-post military exercise was hosted by Russia in September 2022 in its Eastern Military District. "Vostok" means "East" in Russian. (वोस्तोक-2022 — रूस)

• India participated with an Army contingent, along with China and several other countries.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India–Russia bilateral exercises: INDRA (tri-services), AVIAINDRA (air force) and INDRA NAVY.

• Other important Indian exercises: Yudh Abhyas (USA), Malabar (India–USA–Japan–Australia), Varuna (France), Garuda (France, air), Nomadic Elephant (Mongolia), Mitra Shakti (Sri Lanka), Surya Kiran (Nepal), Hand-in-Hand (China).

NOTE

• "Vostok" is also famous as the name of the Soviet spacecraft Vostok 1, in which Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space (12 April 1961).

question: Cultivation of rice needs high rainfall with _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is High temperature and high humidity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rice is a kharif (tropical) crop that requires high temperature (above 25°C), high humidity and rainfall above 100 cm. In areas of lower rainfall it is grown with the help of irrigation. (धान — उच्च तापमान एवं उच्च आर्द्रता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Rice is the staple food of the eastern and southern parts of India. Major producing states: West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar and Tamil Nadu.

• West Bengal is generally the largest producer of rice in India; Punjab and Haryana achieve the highest yields through irrigation.

NOTE

• Kharif crops (sown with the monsoon, June–July; harvested September–October): rice, maize, jowar, bajra, cotton, groundnut. Rabi crops (sown October–December; harvested April–June): wheat, barley, gram, mustard, peas.

question: Which among the following gases is used as an anaesthetic in dental surgery?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitrous Oxide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nitrous Oxide (N₂O)", popularly called "laughing gas", is used as a mild anaesthetic and analgesic in dental surgery and minor operations. (नाइट्रस ऑक्साइड — हास्य गैस)

• It produces a feeling of euphoria and relieves anxiety and pain, while the patient stays conscious.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Radon is a radioactive noble gas produced from the decay of radium; it is a health hazard, not an anaesthetic.

• Argon is an inert gas used in electric bulbs and welding; Helium is used in balloons/airships and, mixed with oxygen, for deep-sea divers and asthma patients.

NOTE

• Nitrous oxide is also a greenhouse gas and is used as a propellant in whipped-cream dispensers and as an oxidiser in rocket and racing engines. Chloroform and ether were the earlier surgical anaesthetics.

question: Who among the following succeeded the throne of the Mughal Dynasty in India after Akbar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jahangir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jahangir (Nur-ud-din Muhammad Salim) succeeded his father Akbar to the Mughal throne in 1605 and ruled till 1627. (अकबर के उत्तराधिकारी — जहाँगीर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Order of the Great Mughals: Babur (1526) → Humayun → Akbar (1556) → Jahangir (1605) → Shah Jahan (1628) → Aurangzeb (1658–1707).

• Jahangir married Mehr-un-Nissa (Nur Jahan) in 1611; he set up the famous "Chain of Justice (Zanjir-i-Adl)" at Agra Fort and wrote the memoir "Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri".

• The English ambassadors Captain William Hawkins and Sir Thomas Roe visited his court.

NOTE

• Sher Shah Suri was not a Mughal — he defeated Humayun at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540) and founded the Sur dynasty, building the Grand Trunk Road and introducing the silver Rupiya.

question: Who among the following Governor Generals of Bengal outlawed the practice of Sati?
solution_text:
The correct answer is William Bentinck.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord William Bentinck, Governor-General of Bengal, abolished the practice of Sati through Regulation XVII of 4 December 1829, making it a punishable offence. (सती प्रथा का अंत — लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिक, 1829)

• The reform was strongly supported by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, the father of the Indian Renaissance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bentinck also suppressed thuggee (with William Sleeman) and female infanticide, and adopted English as the medium of higher education (1835) following Macaulay's Minute.

• Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (1774); Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement (1793) and is called the "Father of Civil Services in India"; Lord Canning was the last Governor-General and the first Viceroy of India (Revolt of 1857).

NOTE

• Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833. Other social reforms: Widow Remarriage Act, 1856 (Lord Canning, inspired by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar).

question: Padma Subrahmanyam received Padma Bhushan Award for her contribution to Indian Classical dance form in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2003.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The eminent Bharatanatyam dancer and researcher Padma Subrahmanyam was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 2003 for her contribution to Indian classical dance. (पद्म सुब्रह्मण्यम — पद्म भूषण, 2003)

• She had earlier received the Padma Shri (1981) and was later awarded the Padma Vibhushan (2024).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• She is known for reviving the "Karanas" described in Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra and for developing the dance form "Bharata Nrityam".

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, one of the eight recognised classical dance forms of India.

NOTE

• Order of civilian awards: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. They were instituted in 1954 and are announced on Republic Day.

question: In India, Gir forest is the last remaining habitat of which animal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asiatic Lion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gir Forest National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary in Gujarat (Junagadh/Gir Somnath region) is the last remaining natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica) in the world. (गिर — एशियाई सिंह का अंतिम प्राकृतिक आवास)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Gir was declared a wildlife sanctuary in 1965; the Asiatic Lion is listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List, and its population has steadily grown in recent lion censuses.

• The Asiatic Lion is smaller than the African lion and has a distinctive longitudinal fold of skin on the belly.

NOTE

• Snow leopards are found in the Himalayas (Ladakh, Himachal, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal) — Hemis National Park is famous for them; the Asiatic Cheetah became extinct in India in 1952, and African cheetahs were reintroduced at Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh, in 2022 under Project Cheetah.

question: In the product method for measurement of national income, we need to deduct the value of intermediate goods to _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is avoid double counting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the product (value added / output) method of measuring national income, the value of intermediate goods is deducted from the value of output so as to avoid double counting — otherwise the same value would be counted more than once at each stage of production. (दोहरी गणना से बचने के लिए)

• Value Added = Value of Output – Value of Intermediate Consumption. Only final goods and services are counted in national income.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The three methods of measuring national income are the Product (Value Added) Method, Income Method and Expenditure Method — all three should give the same total.

• Example: if wheat worth ₹100 becomes flour worth ₹150 and then bread worth ₹200, counting all three (₹450) would be double counting; only the final value ₹200 (or the sum of the value added: 100 + 50 + 50) is correct.

NOTE

• In India, national income estimates are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). The National Income Committee (1949) was chaired by P. C. Mahalanobis.

question: Article 43B of the Indian constitution provide for ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Promotion of cooperative societies.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 43B of the Constitution directs the State to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control and professional management of cooperative societies. (अनुच्छेद 43B — सहकारी समितियों का संवर्धन)

• It was inserted by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011, as a Directive Principle of State Policy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The same amendment added Part IX-B (Articles 243ZH to 243ZT) on cooperative societies and made forming cooperative societies a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(c).

• Other DPSPs in the options: Article 40 — organisation of village panchayats; Article 41 — right to work, education and public assistance; Article 50 — separation of the judiciary from the executive.

NOTE

• DPSPs (Articles 36–51) are borrowed from the Irish Constitution; they are non-justiciable but fundamental in the governance of the country. A separate Ministry of Cooperation was created in 2021.

question: What is the chemical name of Vinegar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acetic Acid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vinegar is a dilute (about 5–8%) solution of acetic acid (CH₃COOH) in water; hence its chemical name is acetic acid (ethanoic acid). (सिरका — एसिटिक अम्ल)

• Pure (100%) acetic acid is called "glacial acetic acid" because it freezes into an ice-like solid at about 16.6°C.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Common acids and their sources: citric acid — citrus fruits (lemon, orange); lactic acid — curd/milk; malic acid — apples; oxalic acid — tomato, spinach; tartaric acid — tamarind, grapes; formic acid — ant sting; butyric acid — rancid butter.

• Lauric acid is a saturated fatty acid found in coconut oil.

NOTE

• Vinegar is widely used as a food preservative and flavouring agent (pickles). Acetic acid is a weak acid and turns blue litmus red.

question: Simone Biles is associated with which sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gymnastics.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Simone Biles of the United States is one of the greatest artistic gymnasts of all time, holding the record for the most World Championship medals in gymnastics. (सिमोन बाइल्स — जिम्नास्टिक्स)

• She won four gold medals at the Rio Olympics, 2016, and several skills in gymnastics are officially named after her (the "Biles").

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Artistic gymnastics events for women: vault, uneven bars, balance beam and floor exercise; for men: floor, pommel horse, rings, vault, parallel bars and horizontal bar.

• Gymnastics is governed by the International Gymnastics Federation (FIG), the oldest international sports federation (founded 1881).

NOTE

• India's best-known gymnast is Dipa Karmakar, who finished fourth in the vault at the Rio 2016 Olympics and is famous for performing the extremely difficult Produnova vault.
